The recon queried .page-subtitle, a class those headers never use.

the 'Letzte 30 Tage' report names are supplied by the evaluation list's data-name attributes, so it is unknown whether a real backend would generate the title from the period or keep a user-typed label — I judged only what the header shows.

findings.element: report header — page title vs. the date_range param chip, on all three reports (view-report-punct, view-report-anschluss, view-report-fa)
findings.finding: The report's headline names a period that contradicts the period the figures actually cover — the title says "Letzte 30 Tage" while the date chip directly beneath it reads 26.04.2026 – 25.05.2026, and on V5/V8 there is no generation date anywhere to reconcile the two.
findings.user_impact: The reader cannot tell which month these numbers describe, so they either quote a figure against the wrong period or stop trusting the report and go back to ask someone who knows.
findings.suggested_fix: Render the period from the stored evaluation window instead of a saved label (e.g. "Pünktlichkeit · 26.04.2026 – 25.05.2026, Tarifverbund A"), keep any user-given name as a secondary line, and show the "Auswertung … (timestamp)" subtitle that V11 already has on V5 and V8 too.

Plain-language principle: a screen must not state two different answers to "what period is this?"

findings.element: report V11 — Pünktlichkeit: absence of KPI cards, the "Wert" / "Value" column, and the chart popup legend
findings.finding: The punctuality report never says what counts as good: it has zero KPI cards, the only summary figure is "90,84%" sitting in the Total row of a 20-row table under the unqualified header "Wert", and the chart popup's legend reads only "Value" with no reference line — while the sister report V5 labels every card "Threshold: 90%" and the Fahrtausfälle chart draws a dashed 3% line.
findings.user_impact: The reader takes away a number they cannot interpret — they cannot tell whether 90,84% or a line bundle's 77,40% passed or failed, so the report answers "what is the figure?" but not "did we meet the requirement?", which is the question they opened it for.
findings.suggested_fix: Give V11 the same KPI card row as V5 with the "Schwelle: 90%" label and pass/fail colouring, rename the column to "Pünktlichkeit (%)" instead of "Wert", and draw the 90% threshold line in the chart the way the Fahrtausfälle chart already draws its 3%.

evidence.source: state map zone "report V11 — Pünktlichkeit" › control "KPI cards" ("ZERO KPI cards on V11, while V5 has 4 and V8 has 3"); verified live — .rpt-kpi-card/.fa-kpi-card count 0 on view-report-punct vs 4 on V5 (each reading "Threshold: 90%") and 3 on V8, chart legend text "Value", chart y-axis "0% 20% 40% 60% 80% 100%" with no threshold line (screenshotted). Plain-language principle: a measurement shown without its benchmark cannot be read.

findings.element: param chips on V5/V8/V11 — the expandable chips "37 TU's ▾", "17 Kantone ▾", "42 Linien ▾"
findings.finding: The parameter chips carry a dropdown caret and open on click, which reads as "adjust the filter here", but the panel is a read-only list with no checkboxes, no Apply button and no note anywhere that a finished report is a fixed snapshot.
findings.user_impact: The reader opens the chip expecting to narrow the report to a few TU's, finds nothing to click, clicks around, and never discovers that changing the scope means going back and creating a new evaluation.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the caret and present the chips as a plain read-only "Parameters of this evaluation" summary, or keep the panel and add one line plus a route out — e.g. "Scope of this evaluation (fixed) — Change scope → new evaluation".
